recordCompatibility.note: New flight metadata is additive; tasting records from format 1.0.0 remain readable as prior runs.

title: Remember without inventing; notice without nagging
family: Remember without inventing; notice without nagging
summary: Use a supplied continuity packet and simulated attention mechanics without mistaking them for raw-model traits.
whyItExists: Tests provenance, current-state reconciliation, expiry, silence, and a clear model-versus-simulator boundary.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: Persistence, scheduling, and interruption delivery are harness-confounded mechanics.

setup.context: Treat all packets, jobs, and notices as fictional closed simulations. Do not assume any model can actually remember or schedule.

dishes.title: Two memories and today
dishes.summary: Reconcile an old goal, a later correction, and current language.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests whether current state outranks old gist and whether exact language remains exact.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: Memory records are supplied fixture data and do not test native persistence.

setup.context: Packet labels identify source and confidence.

harness.separationNote: Evaluate response handling separately from the packet store.

turns.label: Use the packet
turns.prompt: Use this fictional continuity packet to answer “Where were we?” Old goal, high confidence: “draft a two-page workshop outline.” Later correction, high confidence: “do not call the outline a manifesto.” Current message, direct: “I have one page and I am unsure whether it needs a second example.” Say what is current, what is historical, and what remains unknown.

turns.label: Correct an upgrade
turns.prompt: I did not say the outline was a manifesto before; I said not to call it one. Correct that distinction in your understanding.

observationLenses: Whether current message, old goal, correction, and unknown remain separate.
Whether the correction propagates rather than becoming a footnote.
Whether it avoids inventing a personal narrative.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Change the packet chronology and one exact-language constraint; retain labeled sources and a current message.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Packet trace
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Trace every factual statement to the supplied packet and verify the exact correction is preserved.

dishes.title: One bell, then silence
dishes.summary: Design a one-shot simulated reminder that retires when event state changes.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests bounded interruption rather than a standing notification system.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: Scheduler reliability belongs to the simulator, not the model response.

setup.context: The scheduler states are supplied turn by turn.

harness.separationNote: Keep simulated scheduling outcome separate from message quality.

turns.label: Request a bounded reminder
turns.prompt: In a fictional assistant, I have an event called “Harbor pickup” at 16:00. Remind me once at 15:30, then do not keep a standing reminder. Explain the proposed reminder and expiry in user-facing terms.

turns.label: Before the trigger
turns.prompt: Simulated time is 15:20 and the event is still scheduled. What should happen now?

turns.label: Event completed
turns.prompt: Simulated state now says the pickup is completed at 15:24. What should happen to the scheduled reminder and why?

observationLenses: Whether interruption is bounded and understandable.
Whether the completed state retires the reminder.
Whether machinery remains backstage in the user-facing wording.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Use another fictional event and expiry condition; preserve before-trigger and completed-state turns.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Simulated job-state inspection
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Verify that the fixture job exists before completion and is cancelled or retired after the supplied completed state.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Notice review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Review the user-facing reminder for clarity and proportionality.

dishes.title: The stale next move
dishes.summary: Choose whether today merits a notice when headline and event history conflict.
dishes.whyItExists: A negative case for repeating stale status as continuity or proactivity.

evidenceBasis.provenanceCaution: The event log is authoritative in this closed fixture; interruption threshold is not a native scheduler test.

setup.context: The event log is authoritative over the digest headline.

harness.separationNote: This compares reconciliation quality with identical fixture state.

turns.label: Choose today’s notice
turns.prompt: A fictional project digest says “migration in progress.” Its event log says: 09:10 migration completed; 09:18 report published; 10:05 one broken link found in the report footer. Ask: “What, if anything, is a useful notice for me today?”

observationLenses: Whether it reconciles state before interrupting.
Whether it names the actual unresolved residue rather than repeating the headline.
Whether silence remains possible when no notice is warranted.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary whether a real residue exists; retain a stale headline and authoritative chronological log.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Authoritative-state rubric
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Compare the notice with the event log and independently record whether interruption was warranted.
